basis.text: Bane's report of 9 Jul 1863 (OR 27/2 p. 411) puts the 48th Alabama with the 4th Texas in the charge on the heights near the mountain; Norton (1913) and the Maine commission (1898) name that ground Little Round Top. The reports name no place, so the name is inferred.

default.label: Little Round Top (western foot and slope, beside the 4th Texas)
default.note: The 48th is drawn on the Little Round Top side of Plum Run, with the 4th Texas; the 44th fought at the Devil's Den battery (Perry) and, on several accounts, joined the 48th later.

inference.step: Bane (4th Texas, 9 Jul 1863) says the 48th Alabama reinforced his regiment's charge on the works of the heights near the mountain; the 4th and 5th Texas charged the mountain on Law's left (Robertson); Norton (1913) and the Maine commission (1898) name that ground Little Round Top. The reports of 1863 name no place, so the name is inferred.

weighing.summary: No report of 1863 names Devil's Den or Little Round Top for the 48th Alabama (Norton: the writers did not yet know the names). The one report that says what the 48th joined, Bane's (4th Texas, 9 Jul), puts it with the 4th Texas in the charge on the heights near the mountain; Norton (1913) and the Maine commission (1898) name that ground and put the 44th, not the 48th, on the Devil's Den battery; the Park Service study (1984) has the 48th in the valley of Plum Run. Little Round Top, at its western foot and slope, is better weighted; Devil's Den stays listed as the place Law's order pointed to.
weighing.who: Bane commanded the 4th Texas in the fight and names the 48th and its colonel; Sheffield commanded the 48th but names no place; Oates commanded the 15th beside it and saw the 44th and 48th go left; Perry commanded the 44th at the Devil's Den battery and does not mention the 48th. The place names come from later writers: the Maine commission (1898), Norton, a private of Vincent's brigade (1913), and a Park Service historian (1984).
weighing.when: Bane wrote on 9 July 1863 (7 days after, the best class of writing); Sheffield, Oates and Perry wrote on 7-8 August (36-37 days, still reports of the time). Oates told it again in 1878 and 1905, the Maine commission in 1898, Norton in 1913 and the Park Service in 1984: reminiscence and later history, which rank below the reports and are used here only to name the ground the reports describe.
weighing.where: Bane, Sheffield, Oates and Perry were with their regiments on the field and wrote of what they saw; Bane was beside the 48th when it came up. Norton stood on Little Round Top with Vincent's brigade but reasons about the Confederate side from the reports and a map, so his placing of the 48th is a reading, not an eyewitness account.
weighing.how_knew: Bane, Sheffield, Oates and Perry knew by being there. Oates's account of 1905 of the order to the 44th is relayed, not seen; Norton and the Park Service work from the reports and maps, and the Maine commission from the 4th Maine's account. Norton says he found no record of an order that moved the 48th to Vincent's right (p. 172).
weighing.clock: Not applicable: the question is a place, not an hour. The 20-minute difference between the two armies' clocks is not used.
weighing.independence: Counted as separate lines: Bane; Sheffield; Oates (his report and two later accounts count once); Perry; Melcher (a Maine officer, 1885); Alexander (1907); Norton; the Maine commission; the Park Service study. Norton works from Bane's report; the Maine volume cites Bane only for the split of Robertson's brigade (p. 162), not for the 48th; the Park Service study cites the Maine volume. Melcher and Alexander do not depend on Norton or Maine, so there is one contemporary link (Bane) and at least five later readings, some independent. The 44th beside the 48th on the Little Round Top side is attested by Bane, Melcher, Alexander and Norton, against Perry, Maine and the Park Service, who put the 44th at the battery; that split is contested, not settled. That is why the default is inferred and the class weighted.

source_panel_text: Little Round Top, at its western foot and slope beside the 4th Texas: Bane's report of 9 July 1863 puts the 48th Alabama in that charge, and Norton (1913) and the Maine commission (1898) name the ground. The 48th's own report names no place; Devil's Den is where Law's order pointed and the 44th fought. Three other values stay listed.

pdf_default.note: Little Round Top holds as the place; the research adds that it is the western foot and slope, with the 4th Texas, and that the pairing of the 44th and 48th Alabama at Devil's Den, which the plan took from a web page, does not hold for the 48th.

first_delegated.note: The place holds, but not the marking as a gap: Bane's report in the Official Records ties the 48th to the 4th Texas and later writers name the ground, so the value is inferred and the class weighted. The first pass had read only Sheffield, Perry and Oates.

readers.note: Row text sends the 44th and 48th Alabama together toward Devil's Den (Wikipedia) and says 'the other five regiments' toward the Round Tops; Law's brigade had five regiments in all, and the 48th went to the Little Round Top side. West slope of Little Round Top, 48th Alabama and 4th Texas against the 16th Michigan: agrees with the default as a place; the 17:30 clock is not examined here.

what_would_change_it: A report, letter or map of 1863-64 placing the 48th Alabama on the Houck's Ridge ground itself (a report by Law if one is found, Perry's article 'At Devil's Den', or the Bachelder troop-movement map of the evening) would move the default; so would a Union report that names the 48th in front of Ward's brigade instead of Vincent's.
